findings.issue: finish() sends SIGKILL to -child.pid after the child has already exited and been reaped. If the group has emptied, that PGID is free, and in theory a new unrelated process could have taken the same PID and made itself a group leader (setsid/setpgid) before the kill. That process would then be killed. In practice the gap is microseconds, the target would need to be a fresh group leader with exactly that PID, and the runner VM is single-use. So this is defence in depth only, with no realistic path.
findings.evidence: child 'exit' event -> finish() -> killGroup(child.pid, 'SIGKILL') -> process.kill(-pid). No untrusted input controls the PID or the timing.
findings.fix: Optional: accept the risk and keep the comment, or note in it that a lingering descendant keeps the PGID reserved, so the kill hits either our own group or nothing in all but a vanishingly small reuse window.

findings.issue: killGroup rethrows anything other than ESRCH. If every member left in the group is root-owned (e.g. apt under sudo after npx has exited), kill(-pgid) returns EPERM. That throws from a timer or event callback, which is an uncaught exception, so the helper crashes. The step still fails (non-zero exit), so this fails closed and is not a vulnerability. The cost is an unclear error and no retry.
findings.evidence: sudo apt in the attempt's group -> timeout or finish -> process.kill(-pid) -> EPERM -> throw inside a setTimeout or 'exit' handler -> process crash.
findings.fix: Optional: also tolerate EPERM (log it as a warning) so the retry loop carries on, or leave as is, since it fails closed.

summary: No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings. Arguments come only from the checked-in ci.yml (constant label, flags and command) and are passed to spawn as an argv array without a shell, so there is no command injection. No event data (PR title, branch name) reaches the helper or the run lines. Signals go only to -child.pid, the group the helper created with detached:true; never 0 or -1, and never with an undefined PID. The SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers are removed in finally. Option parsing uses strict parseArgs and rejects stray positionals and non-finite or invalid numbers. Workflow permissions stay contents: read, no new actions or secrets, no new dependencies. The logged command line and the ::warning::/::error:: messages contain only constants and errno messages. The test fixture writes only into per-test mkdtemp state files.
